meta.title: Sources added by decision-hub
meta.method: Each URL below was opened and its content read on 2026-11-12 from this session. Where a page could not be fetched by the sandbox, the row says so and the page is not relied upon for a value.

sources.label: NFL.com — official injury report (Week 10 of the 2026 season at the time of reading)
sources.note: Page title read on 2026-11-12: 'Official Latest NFL Injury Report for Players - Week 10 of the 2026 Season'. Renders game-day grouping, player, position, injury, practice status and game status. Dynamic page; values change during the week.

sources.label: NFL.com — 2026 Week 10 injury report (dated URL)
sources.note: Same content as the live page for that week; the dated URL is cited so the snapshot can be found again. Read 2026-11-12; the in-page heading said 'WEEK 10', matching both the title and the URL (earlier sessions recorded a title/body disagreement in week 7/8 that does not reproduce here).

sources.label: nflreadr — load_injuries() reference and column list
sources.note: Documents the injury feed: season, game_type, team, week, gsis_id, position, full_name, report_primary_injury, report_secondary_injury, report_status, practice_primary_injury, practice_secondary_injury, practice_status. States data available since 2009 and that the feed is collected from the league's injury-report API. Used to confirm the column names this project parses.

sources.label: nflreadr — data dictionary, depth charts (2025+ schema)
sources.note: Documents dt (ISO-8601 load timestamp), team, player_name, gsis_id, pos_grp, pos_name, pos_abb, pos_slot, pos_rank. States the source changed after the 2024 season, so the 2026 schema is the one described. Confirms pos_rank is rank grouped by pos_slot, which is why this project computes its own ordinal within (team, position).

sources.label: nflreadr — data dictionary, rosters
sources.note: Documents status (Active, Inactive, Injured Reserve, Practice Squad), depth_chart_position, gsis_id and pfr_id. The pfr_id is what lets the snap-count feed (which has no GSIS id) be joined to players.

sources.label: nflreadr — data dictionary, snap counts
sources.note: Documents offense_pct and defense_pct and confirms the file has pfr_player_id but no gsis_id. This is why the tracker joins through the roster's pfr_id and reports how many snap rows had no crosswalk.

sources.label: nflverse-data — release index (injuries, depth_charts, weekly_rosters, snap_counts)
sources.note: Consulted through the GitHub API on 2026-11-12: depth_charts_2026.csv is 74,128,321 bytes updated 2026-11-12T07:01:41Z; injuries_2026.csv is 349,835 bytes; roster_weekly_2026.csv is 8,022,368 bytes; snap_counts_2026.csv is 1,139,048 bytes. The derived build records the SHA-256 of each file it consumed.
sources.verified_by: GitHub API queried 2026-11-12 in this session

sources.label: operations.nfl.com — injury-report policy page (returns 404)
sources.note: Re-checked 2026-11-12: HTTP 404 with the body '404 - FLAG ON THE PLAY'. The root project cites this URL as its injury-policy source. The page's absence is recorded as a flag (FL-DH-05) rather than worked around; no secondary summary of the policy is relied upon for a rule.

sources.label: Official injury report feed used by the tracker (2026 CSV release asset)
sources.org: nflverse (community mirror of the league's injury-report API)
sources.note: The exact asset the fetch workflow downloads. 3,075 rows for 2026 at the 2026-11-12 snapshot. Because it is a mirror, the tracker also cites the league's own page for the same week, and the two are compared on the injuries page.
sources.verified_by: downloaded by the fetch-injuries workflow run 43223996079 on 2026-11-12

sources.label: Club depth charts feed used by the tracker (2026 CSV release asset)
sources.org: nflverse (community mirror of club-supplied depth charts)
sources.note: 777,815 rows for 2026, 291 distinct snapshots; the newest snapshot at build time was 2026-11-12T07:01:31Z. Depth charts are club-supplied and are not an official NFL publication — the site says so wherever a rank is displayed.
sources.verified_by: downloaded by the fetch-injuries workflow on 2026-11-12

sources.label: Weekly rosters feed (status and PFR crosswalk)
sources.note: Used for roster status (ACT/INA/RES...) and for the pfr_id to gsis_id crosswalk. 24,549 rows for 2026.
sources.verified_by: downloaded by the fetch-injuries workflow on 2026-11-12

sources.label: Snap counts feed (playing time by player-week)
sources.note: 12,693 rows for 2026; 2,372 had no PFR crosswalk to a GSIS id and are excluded from the snap-share field, which is reported in the dataset's own metadata rather than hidden.
sources.verified_by: downloaded by the fetch-injuries workflow on 2026-11-12

sources.label: This repository — the independent audit implementation
sources.note: The code that produces every check and flag on the audit page. It imports nothing from the root pipeline, so agreement is evidence and disagreement is a finding.
sources.verified_by: run in this session; output committed as decision-hub/data/root_audit.json

sources.label: This repository — the injury/depth fetch and rank builder
sources.note: The code that produces decision-hub/data/injuries.json, including the within-position ordinal that replaces the feed's per-slot pos_rank.
sources.verified_by: executed by the fetch-injuries GitHub workflow on 2026-11-12

sources.label: NFL.com — NFL extends strategic partnership with Genius Sports (official data distribution)
sources.note: Establishes that official NFL data is distributed to sportsbooks through a commercial partner, which is why no official public feed of historical betting prices exists for a project like this one.
sources.verified_by: carried over from the root source register, which records reading it on 2026-11-01
